 We are seeking an experienced Project Engineer to support the delivery of a large-scale civil infrastructure project involving bulk earthworks, utilities, roads, drainage and associated subdivision works.
 Working closely with the Project Manager and site delivery team, you will play a key role in coordinating subcontractors, managing consultant and design interfaces, resolving technical queries and ensuring works are delivered safely, efficiently and in accordance with project requirements.
 The role will involve significant coordination between site teams, subcontractors, design consultants and external stakeholders to ensure design documentation, approvals and construction activities remain aligned with the project programme.
 This is an excellent opportunity to join a growing contractor with a strong pipeline of work across Western Sydney.
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
 - Coordinate day-to-day project delivery activities across multiple work fronts.
 - Manage subcontractors, suppliers, consultants and design interfaces.
 - Coordinate with civil, structural, services and other design consultants to resolve technical and construction-related issues.
 - Manage subcontractor RFIs, technical queries and design clarifications, ensuring timely responses from relevant consultants.
 - Support design management activities, including design reviews, documentation coordination, constructability assessments and design changes.
 - Monitor design deliverables, approvals and outstanding information to ensure construction activities remain on programme.
 - Prepare and manage RFIs, NCRs, ITPs, SWMS reviews and project documentation.
 - Monitor programme, productivity and project milestones.
 - Assist with procurement, scope packages and subcontractor management.
 - Track project costs, variations and progress claims.
 - Support quality assurance and compliance activities across site.
 - Liaise with client representatives, authorities and key project stakeholders.
 - Prepare regular project reporting and progress updates.
 - Drive efficient project outcomes through proactive problem solving and coordination.
 SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
 - Experience as a Project Engineer within civil infrastructure, subdivisions or earthworks projects.
 - Strong understanding of bulk earthworks, roads, drainage and utility installation.
 - Demonstrated experience coordinating engineering consultants and managing design-related issues during construction.
 - Ability to manage subcontractor RFIs, technical queries and design documentation.
 - Experience reviewing construction drawings, identifying design discrepancies and coordinating practical solutions.
 - Strong subcontractor management, project documentation and stakeholder coordination skills.
 - Ability to manage competing priorities across multiple work fronts in a live construction environment.
 - Strong communication, organisational and problem-solving skills.
 - Proficient with project management and reporting systems such as Procore, Laminar or similar.
 - Relevant Civil Engineering qualification.
 THE OPPORTUNITY
 - Major infrastructure project within the Western Sydney Airport growth corridor.
 - Long-term project pipeline and strong job security.
 - Exposure to large-scale civil infrastructure and subdivision works.
 - Broad involvement across engineering, design coordination and construction delivery.
 - High-performing and collaborative project team.
 - Genuine career progression opportunities.
 THE DETAILS
 - Full-time, site-based position.
 - Western Sydney location.
 - Competitive salary package based on experience.
 - Immediate start available.
 HOW TO APPLY
 Apply now or contact us for a confidential discussion about the opportunity.

With award-winning capabilities in dredging, civil contracting, and marine engineering, they pride themselves on their expertise in project management and their strong commitment to clients, employees, and the wider community.

candidates.content_text:
Help shape stormwater’s next chapter.
You’ve built your technical skills. You’re ready to take on more responsibility, contribute your ideas and develop the confidence to lead.
Rain Consulting is looking for a Project Engineer or Scientist with 3 to 7 years’ relevant experience to join our Melbourne team.
We’re a specialist stormwater and surface water consultancy. We plan and design better water environments, investigate how water behaves and help clients turn complex information into decisions they can act on.
Our purpose
At Rain, we exist to support, challenge and lift ourselves, each other and the people we work with.
That means helping clients understand their options and giving them the clarity and confidence to act. It also means backing our own people to develop their judgement, take ownership and contribute to how the industry works.
We value creative thinking, especially when it leads to a sound, practical solution.
How we work
Our values guide our decisions and the standards we hold ourselves to:
- Quality: We check assumptions, review our work and explain the findings clearly.
- Integrity: We give honest advice, including when a client needs to hear something difficult.
- Stewardship: We consider what our decisions mean for communities and the environment over the long term.
You’ll work with major clients, including City of Melbourne and Melbourne Water, as part of a small team where your contribution is visible.
You’ll have direct support from Luke and Rianda, Rain’s Directors, and colleagues who want to see you develop. As your capability grows, there’s room to take on greater responsibility and build your own voice in the industry.
We welcome questions, thoughtful challenges and ideas for doing things better. You’ll be trusted to contribute, with technical review and support around you.
The role is Melbourne-based with hybrid working and flexibility, within a team that looks out for each other.
The problems you’ll help solve
A council is rethinking how it manages water across its community. A wetland or waterway needs a design that supports both people and the environment. A project needs a water balance to understand where water comes from, where it goes and how it could be used.

These are the kinds of questions you’ll work through at Rain.
You’ll use TUFLOW and RORB to investigate how water behaves, test options and understand their consequences. Your projects may also involve wetland and waterway design, water balances and integrated water management. You’ll turn that work into clear maps, reports and conversations that help people make sound decisions.
You’ll also get involved beyond the technical analysis. From shaping the brief to discussing the findings with the client, you’ll develop an understanding of what makes a project useful, achievable and worth doing. That includes managing scope, budgets and deadlines, with support from the team.

As your confidence and capability grow, you’ll have opportunities to take greater ownership, guide others and contribute to our training or facilitation work.
The aim is for your contribution to keep helping people long after the report is delivered.
What you’ll bring
- An Engineering degree, including civil or environmental engineering, or an Environmental Science degree.
- 3 to 7 years’ relevant experience in flood, stormwater or water management.
- Solid practical TUFLOW and RORB skills.
- An understanding of hydrologic, hydraulic and stormwater processes.
- The ability to plan your work, take responsibility and ask for support when you need it.
- Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain technical findings to different audiences.
- Curiosity about better ways of doing things and care for the quality and impact of your work.
Experience with MUSIC and QGIS is valuable. Training, facilitation or mentoring experience is a bonus.
Your next move
Send your CV and a short note about why you’d like to work at Rain to hiring@rainconsulting.com.au.
Tell us about the work you’ve done, the work you’d like to do next and what you’d bring to the team.
You’re also welcome to email us if you’d like to ask a question before applying.
We welcome applications from people with different backgrounds and experiences.

Our client is a well-established and growing engineering consultancy based in Pyrmont, specialising in remedial engineering, façade remediation and structural rehabilitation projects.

- Assist with structural assessments and engineering calculations
- Support the preparation of technical reports and remedial scopes of work

- Coordinate with engineers, consultants and contractors

- Excellent attention to detail

- Learn directly from experienced structural and remedial engineers

- Opportunity to gain both office-based and practical site experience
- Diverse projects across residential and commercial buildings

candidates.content_text:
Why work with Goldstate Homes
At Goldstate Homes, we build across a wider range of residential markets than most builders: investment homes, knockdown rebuilds, dual occupancies, townhouses, SDA homes, co-living properties, Class 1b rooming houses, dual key homes and turnkey house and land packages. For our team, that means varied and challenging work. No two projects are quite the same, and you'll keep building your skills and experience across many building types. We pride ourselves on speed, service and quality, and we build every home as if it were our own. Our people take real ownership of their work and can see what they've contributed to every home we deliver. If you want to grow your career in a close-knit team that cares about doing things properly, Goldstate Homes is a great place to be.
The role
We're looking for an experienced Production Draftsperson to join the team. Reporting to the Drafting Manager, you'll prepare detailed, accurate working drawings from our current portfolio and custom homes. You'll take each job from sales plans through to construction-ready documentation.
Your day-to-day will include:
- Preparing production and working drawings in Revit.
- Applying client variations, site-specific changes, engineering and developer requirements to drawings
- Checking that plans comply with the NCC, council and regulatory body requirements
- Working with our BDM, Estimating, Contract Admin and Construction teams to provide technical support for client and agent queries
- Liaising with Building Surveyors, Engineers, Councils and Town Planners
- Keeping templates, standards and drawing sets consistent and up to date
About you
- At least 3 years' demonstrated experience as a production draftsperson in volume or custom residential building
- A thorough working knowledge of the NCC and residential construction methods
- Intermediate to advanced Revit skills (essential)
- Strong attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy
- Good problem-solving skills and the ability to find practical solutions
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills
- Ability to manage your workload and meet deadlines
- A team player who does well in a supportive, close-knit environment
What we offer
- Working with a friendly, close-knit team where your contribution is valued
- Varied work across both volume and custom residential projects
- Support and guidance from an experienced Drafting Manager
- Opportunities for professional development and career growth
- Be part of an established and growing residential building company
- A competitive salary

candidates.content_text:
A career with Bega Valley Shire Council offers the opportunity to engage in meaningful and diverse work that supports the vibrant communities of the south-east corner of NSW. Nestled between rolling hills and some of the state’s most stunning beaches, this region is home to a variety of people who enjoy both rural and coastal living.
As an AR Bluett Award winning Council, we are proud of our dedicated and talented team, whose efforts make our success possible.
With a workforce of over 350, we provide essential services to our communities, including libraries, customer service, finance, children’s services, engineering, project management, road maintenance, water management, environment, parks, gardens, and town centres.
We offer a range of employment benefits to support our staff, which may include:
 - Rostered days off
 - Flexible work arrangements
 - Salary packaging
 - Paid study leave of 3 hours per week (or equivalent over a four-week period)
 - Approved study-related expenses
 The Opportunity
We have an exciting opportunity for a motivated individual to join Councils Emerging Talent Program and undertake a Certificate III in Water Industry Operations while gaining practical experience and mentorship across Council's Water and Sewer Services.
As a Water and Sewer Trainee, you will combine vocational studies with hands-on workplace experience across a range of water and sewer network operations functions, including Water Treatment Operations, Sewerage Treatment Operations, Network Maintenance, and Infrastructure Construction. You will gain practical experience in the operation, monitoring and maintenance of essential water and sewer services while developing the skills, knowledge and qualifications required for a rewarding career in the water industry.
The role may also involve travel and participation in residential training blocks associated with your qualification program.
As a participant in Council's Emerging Talent Program, you will have the opportunity to develop your skills through structured learning, on-the-job experience, mentoring and exposure to a broad range of professional disciplines, building a strong foundation for a successful career in local government and beyond.
Council will support your studies by providing paid study leave of 3 hours per week (or equivalent over a four-week period) together with approved study-related expenses.
Key responsibilities include:
 - Undertake vocational studies and apply theoretical learning to workplace activities to develop practical skills and knowledge.
 - Assist with the operation, monitoring and maintenance of water and sewerage infrastructure and associated systems.
 - Assist in the construction, installation and repair of water supply and sewerage infrastructure.
 - Assist with the maintenance, servicing and cleaning of water and sewer treatment plant and equipment.
 - Develop skills in inspection, fault finding, testing and problem solving across water and sewer networks.
 This role offers valuable exposure to a broad range of water and sewer operations while developing practical skills and experience to support a future career in Water and Sewer Services.
To view the Position Description, please click here. 
About You
We are seeking two (2) individuals who have obtained a School Certificate (Year 10) or equivalent and hold a NSW Class C drivers' licence (or ability to obtain).
You will have the following skills and experience;
 - Demonstrated analytical and investigative ability to assist in resolving operational problems in the field.
 - Ability to participate in the laying, repair and maintenance of water and sewer mains and associated construction activities.
 - Ability to develop fault-finding and troubleshooting skills relevant to water supply and sewerage systems.
 - Well-developed oral and written communication skills.
 - Demonstrated commitment to learning, teamwork and working safely in an operational environment.
 Benefits
This is a fixed term full-time position working 38 hours per week for a period of two (2) years.
The total remuneration package for this position commences at $29,195.71 to $50,115.52 gross per annum, comprising of:
 - $501.30 to 860.50 per week base salary
 - $60.16 to 860.50 per week superannuation (calculated at 12%)
 Remuneration for this position is dependent upon the age and level of schooling achieved by the successful candidate.
Additional benefits for this position include:
 - Rostered day off scheme (nine day fortnight)
 - Paid study leave of up to 3 hours per week (or equivalent over a four-week period)
 - Approved study-related expenses
 - Annual Award salary increases and performance reviews
 - Salary packaging program (SmartSalary)
 - Wellbeing Initiatives – Fitness Passport, Employee Assistance Program, Telus Health App, social club, health monitoring and annual flu vaccinations
 For further information on this position, please contact Luke Cathor - Water and Sewer Networks Operations Coordinator on 0467 787 467.
Applications close 11.59pm AEDT on 22 November 2026.
Applicants must have the right to work in Australia and address the advertised selection criteria demonstrating their suitability for the role.
This position requires applicants to be suitably immunised in line with recommendations from the Australian Immunisation Handbook, mandated Public Health Orders and/or Councils Immunisation Procedure.

Building for Generations through the Pursuit of Excellence
The FKG Construction team has a proud 50+ year history of successfully delivering a variety of commercial construction projects across a wide range of sectors including both government and private clients. We are dedicated to building for generations, achieved through our personable approach with all people, including those within our communities within which we live every day.
We believe our people are the key to our success and we are invested in supporting the wellbeing of our team members, providing skills development opportunities, rewarding performance and recognising high achievement.
As an FKG Group employee you will have access to our range of benefits which includes corporate health insurance discounts, employee assistance program, our “Thrive” wellbeing initiative and many more.
The Role
Keen to kick start your career in the construction industry and work alongside your degree? Then look no further!  Due to recent organisational growth we are looking for our next superstar Cadet!
A cadetship at FKG will give you knowledge across all areas of construction, you'll learn from experienced members of the team, obtain hands-on involvement across a variety of exciting commercial projects and be given excellent learning support and mentorship as you develop your career.
Responsibilities
You will enjoy the variety within your job scope, including:
- Organisation and management of suppliers and subcontractors
- Procurement of trade packages and assistance in developing cost reports;
- Liaison with clients, site staff, design managers, estimators, and project managers
- Estimation, design and contract administration
Experience and Qualifications
 To be considered for this role, you will need:
- To be currently enrolled and successfully completed the first year of your Bachelor of Construction Management/ Urban Development/ Quantity Surveying
- Highly developed organisational, time management and prioritising skills A can-do attitude, self-motivated and willingness to learn;
- An exceptional level of verbal and written communication and interpersonal skills Previous construction industry experience would be an advantage;
- To include your ATAR results on your resume.
Apply Now!
- FKG is an equal opportunity employer, where we recognise the diversity of our team and actively promote equality of opportunity for all with the right mix of talent, skills and potential. We welcome all applications from a wide range of candidates. Selection for roles will be based on individual merit alone.

candidates.abstract: Crucial role in the continued success of UGL Regional Linx safely operating and maintaining the Country Regional Network in regional NSW
candidates.location: Bathurst, Blue Mountains & Central West NSW
bullets: Historic piece of regional NSW rail infrastructure
Excellent long term career prospects
Work in a motivated, inclusive, high performing and flexible environment
candidates.content_text:
About UGL Regional Linx
At UGL Regional Linx (UGLRL), we help connect communities across regional New South Wales by managing and maintaining the Country Regional Network (CRN). As a subsidiary of UGL Transport, we are proud to create meaningful employment opportunities in regional and rural communities, with more than 85% of our workforce based across regional NSW.
We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where people feel valued, supported, and empowered to succeed. Guided by our core values, we foster a culture built on collaboration, respect, safety, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Job Purpose
The Estimator is responsible for preparing project estimates with accurate cost allocations and up to date market knowledge, monitoring the performance of project estimates, managing the change control process associated with project estimates, maintaining the CATS Resource Library with current benchmarked rates, and leading the overall 3MWP estimation process with the support of Infrastructure delivery team subject matter experts, the Procurement team, Finance team, and Assets & Engineering subject matter experts. 
The Estimator supports Project Owners by preparing and updating cost estimates for variations and facilitating the conversion of provisional sums to fixed-cost submissions.
What You'll Be Doing
Be responsible for the estimation of the 3 Year Maintenance Works Program, including the supervision and management of external and internal resources used during the process of estimation
Prepare detailed estimates for every project in the 3MWP in line with the Project Controls Plan process for estimation.
Assist in the preparation of UGLRL Enhancements estimates as required, including the loading of those estimates into CATS
Preparing and updating Estimates for Variations and conversion of Provisional Sum to Fixed Costs submissions
Maintain the UGL Regional Linx CATS Register and Master Resource Library
Maintain up to date Labour, Plant, Material rates within the Master Resource Library
Develop and maintain an “Estimating Manual” for UGLRL Projects. 
Review all project documentation to understand the requirements of the work to include the analysis of technical, contractual and financial requirements.
Explore opportunities for innovation while identifying risk and opportunities.
Maintain accurate and details estimate files.
Maintain awareness of best practice in the industry
Develop innovative estimates and options through knowledge of the latest design and or construction techniques to deliver the best possible outcome for UGLRL
Coordinates and collaborates with subject matter experts on methodology, program, IR, Plant and estimate review processes
Perform trend analysis and actively evaluate project cost and estimate performance
About You
Tertiary qualification in Engineering, Quantity Surveying or similar profession. (Desirable)
3+ years’ experience working in an estimating role
Knowledge of construction, material components, regulations and estimating
Sound knowledge and experience within the rail industry, especially in an O&M context
Ability to read and interpret drawings/plans and specifications
Why Join UGL Regional Linx?
Be part of an organisation that plays a vital role in connecting regional communities.
Work within a supportive and collaborative team environment.
Access opportunities for professional growth and career development.
Contribute to projects with lasting community and infrastructure impact.
Join a business that values diversity, inclusion, and different perspectives.
Diversity & Inclusion
At UGL Regional Linx, we believe diverse teams create better outcomes. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities.
We are particularly committed to increasing female representation across our business and strongly encourage women to apply, even if you don't meet every requirement listed.
We also encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people living with disability, culturally and linguistically diverse candidates, LGBTQIA+ individuals, and mature-age professionals.
Our recruitment process may include national criminal history checks and pre-employment medical assessments, including drug and alcohol screening.

candidates.content_text:
About us
We are a purpose-led construction company dedicated to delivering a landmark regenerative building in Western Australia.
Designed to set a new benchmark for sustainable construction, the project brings together low-carbon materials, renewable energy, and water-sensitive design to create a building that gives back more than it takes.
We work closely with the local community, industry partners, and specialist practitioners, and we share what we learn so others can build better too.
About the role
We are looking for a Site Engineer to join us on an initial 6 month, fixed term contract, with the possibility of extension.
You will provide site-based technical and coordination support to our Construction Manager, Project Manager, and wider project team. Your focus will be on reviewing drawings, finding design errors and discrepancies before they reach construction, coordinating trades, and verifying quality on site.
This role is based on site full time and involves daily site inspections.
We know good people work in different ways and we are open to discussing working arrangements that suit you, including hours, location, and how the week is structured. If there is an arrangement that would work better for you, we are happy to talk it through.
What you will do
- Review construction drawings at each revision, checking dimensions, setouts, levels, and cross-references between architectural, structural, and services documentation.
- Identify discrepancies, clashes, missing details, and buildability issues before work starts, and communicate changes between revisions to the trades they affect.
- Verify shop drawings against design drawings, take part in clash detection and building information modelling (BIM) reviews, and keep a drawing issue register through to closure.
- Keep trade interfaces, sequencing, and deliveries running smoothly with the Site Manager, including access, setout, service penetrations, embedments, and cast-in items.
- Make sure every trade works from current drawings, and escalate any works at risk of proceeding on incorrect or outdated information.
- Confirm setout, dimensions, and quality match the drawings before and during works, through inspection and test plans, hold point and witness inspections, pre-pour checks, and frame checks.
- Collect and verify site records, including moisture readings, cutting and penetration registers, survey checks, material dockets, and test certificates, and track non-conformances and defects through to closure.
- Draft and manage requests for information (RFIs) through to response, with supporting photos, markups, and measurements, and record site instructions and variations arising from design errors, including time and cost impacts.
About you
- Minimum of 5 years' site-based experience on commercial construction projects.
- Demonstrated ability to read and interrogate architectural, structural, and services drawings, with a track record of catching errors before construction.
- Strong setout and dimensional literacy, including levels, grids, and tolerances.
- Experience drafting RFIs and drawing markups.
- Working knowledge of Aconex or an equivalent platform.
- Strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with all stakeholders.
- Sound judgement and initiative, with the ability to anticipate issues, resolve them independently, and escalate appropriately.
- Must hold a current White Card and WA driver's licence.
- High attention to detail, a collaborative approach, and the ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
- Experience on mass timber, structural steel, high specification and exposed services-dense projects is preferred.
- Trade experience or a tertiary qualification in construction management or engineering is preferred but not essential.
- Experience with BIM model review, such as Navisworks, is preferred but not essential.
- Familiarity with AS 3600, AS 3610, or structural tolerance standards is preferred but not essential.
We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences. If you do not tick every box but think you would be great in this role, we would still like to hear from you. We are committed to a fair and accessible recruitment process, please let us know if you need any adjustments to take part.
